Brazos A7 Well A-4 was one of 4 wells on the Brazos A7 Platform that were previously TA?d.  This summary covers only the recent work that was done in March, 2005 to cut and proof-pull the remaining casings in preparation for platform abandonment which is planned for the summer of 2005.  

The work began on Well A-4 on 3/14/05.  The 30-inch, 20-inch, 16-inch, and 11-7/8-inch casings were torch cut and the wellheads were removed.  The 20-inch was just a short piece about 5 feet long with a bell guide on the bottom which fell down about 10 feet into the well when it was cut loose at the surface. (The 9-5/8-inch casing had already been cut and its stub removed in 2004.)  A mechanical pipe cutter was run in the hole and the 11-7/8-inch casing was cut at 25 feet BML.  The 11-7/8-inch stub dropped 4 inches and turned freely so it had to be removed before cutting the next casing could continue.  After removing the 11-7/8? stub, the 16-inch casing was then mechanically cut at 21 feet BML.  It too, fell a few inches and turned.  The 16-inch casing stub was removed from the well.  A spear was then used to pull and remove the 5-foot piece of 20-inch casing with the bell guide on the bottom of it.  The mechanical cutter was picked up again and the 30-inch casing was cut at 18 feet BML.  The cut was completed on 3/23/05.  On 3/24/05, casing jacks were used to pull the 30-inch casing up about 2 feet to prove that the cut was complete.  The 30-inch casing stub was not removed from the well.

Final abandonment is planned for June 2005 when the 30-inch casing stub will be removed along with the entire platform.  Final site clearance will be performed after the platform is removed.

RESTORE  THE  ?MARG A-6?   SAND  TO  PRODUCTION

SUMMARY:   Isolated water/mud influx and restored the Marg A-6 Sand back to production.  
Used Electric Line to isolate the lower perforations of the Marg A-6 Sand by setting a through tubing expandable plug (TTEP) above the lower perforations.   Prior to electric line operations, coiled tubing washed the wellbore down to the PBTD.
DISCUSSION:  The WC 130, Well #3 was completed well as a single, non-gravel packed gas producer in the ?MARG A-6? Sand.  Initial production began on 07/10/2006 at 25,155 MCFPD, 44 BOPD, 41 BWPD on 25/64? with 11,700 psi FTP, SITP = 13,250 psi.
On 9/25/06, the well began making water.  The production rate was reduced from ~30,000 MMCFPD to 25,000 MCFPD and the water rate leveled out at ~300 BWPD.  
On 11/30/06, the well began making mud and fine sand.  The rate was reduced to 5,000 MCFPD but the problem persisted.  The WC 130, #3 is shut in until the lower perforations are isolated.
NOTE:  During the Completion, it was discovered that the 7? production liner was leaking through a connection around 17,100?.  The leaking 7? connection was isolated by setting two cement retainers above the casing failure.  However the bottom of the lower perforations are only 10? above the retainer.  It is likely that the recent influx of water and mud production is coming from the failed casing and has worked its way into the lower perforations.

This possible scenario was discussed with Ben Coco in the Houma District and he advised of the necessary Regional approvals.
   
Due to these 2 conflicting pieces of info, and a long history of low GOR in the C-15, ANKOR received approval to flow test the TP-9 sand to determine content.  If gas, production in the TP-9 sand would be delayed until production in the C-15 oil well watered out, and ANKOR would produce the TP-6 oil sand avoiding production of a gas cap. The intent of the slickline intervention was to dummy up the gas lift valves, change producing zones, and set a packer in the tubing.

The slickline crew made an attempt to shut the lower zone (BS-61) and we believe the sleeves are shifted closed. However, due to the difficulty in shifting the sleeves, the decision was made to rig down.

The difficulties so far have been caused by restrictions in the tubing which have prevented the shifting tools & plugs from falling to the desired depth. Further efforts to shift sleeves with the same size tools could result in the loss of tools in the hole.

As of now there is a XRX type plug set above the SCSSV. We should be able to bleed pressure to our system & eliminate pressure at surface. The well is shut-in and being monitored.

Plan Forward:

The plan forward is to change producing zones and determine if a thru-tubing packer set above the SCSSV can successfully seal and prevent pressure buildup to surface. The BS-61 zone will be isolated with a cast iron bridge plug and cement cap. The BS-58 upper section will be accessed by perforating the tubing to allow flow from said zone around the closed sleeves. A packer with a pump-out plug will then be set in the tubing to test tubing integrity. Note: An RPM has been filed to complete this portion of work in February 2013, and is currently pending approval.

W&T has been conducting a Lube and Bleed program in order to reduce casing pressure on the Intermediate Casing of the OCS G 2354 HI 111 A-11 well. The program introduces heavy weighted mud to the annulus while bleeding lighter mud and gas to reduce the sustained casing pressure to a level within API RP 90 approval requirements or to zero psi. We began with 4000 psi on the annulus and have reduced the pressure to ~ 2650 psi (some of it induced) at which point the Lube and Bleed program was suspended on 5-30-14. Over the course of the Lube and Bleed program we were able to add 14.1 barrels of 17.1 #/gallon heavy mud to the annulus and swap 59.5 barrels of lighter mud to heavy mud. Our annulus mud weights have increased from an initial weight of 9.0-9.5 #/gallon up to 13.6 #/gallon.  We have initiated a pressure monitor program for the next 30 days to determine if sustained casing pressure levels warrant a departure request for SCP or whether repair action is recommended in which case a separate submittal would be required to the District.

In Aug 2015 the DC111 single zone completion had a failed Baker Neptune (Gen-1) SCSSV replaced along with its 5.5-in 23-ppf 13Cr85 Tubing. Prior to removal of the completion tubing string, the SCSSV was locked open and a surveillance run on wireline was made. This consisted of a 3.18-in drift, run on wireline through to the bottom of the sand control screens. This drift run confirmed that there were no blockages / restrictions through the bore of the completion. 

The reservoir was isolated during the SCSSV and Tubing retrieval from the well via a mechanical bridge plug, so as to prevent fluid loss to the formation and possible formation damage. The originally installed upper completion was removed via shearing of the Tubing Shear Latch (TSL) above the originally installed production packer. This left a Polished Bore Receptacle (PBR) above the originally installed Production Packer. This PBR served to receive the new seal assembly that would be installed beneath the new completion tubing string.

A new tapered tubing string was installed consisting of 5.5-in 23-ppf 13Cr85 tubing x 4.5-in 15.1-ppf 13Cr85 tubing. The 5.5-in tubing was only installed from the tubing hanger to the 10 ¾-in Tie-Back crossover on the production casing string. The 4.5-in tubing was installed from the 10 ¾-in Tie-Back crossover through the 9 7/8-in production casing down to the PBR above the TSL. 
The new SCSSV was installed on the 5.5-in completion tubing to a depth of approx. 3,000-ft beneath the mud-line as per Atlantis Completions BOD.  This SCSSV was a Schlumberger TRC-II 10-ksi model with 4.375-in QN nipple profile as per Atlantis Completions BOD.

A new Schlumberger dual redundant gauge mandrel was installed with 2 gauges (redundant) each reading the tubing pressure and temperature. Schlumberger Dual Check Injection Nipples (DCINs) were installed for chemical injection as per Atlantis Completions BOD. A new Baker Premier Production Packer was installed above the TSL PBR. 

The production annulus (Annulus-A) was left with 9.1-ppg CaCl2 packer fluid, the production tubing was left with 6.5-ppg Base Oil. The mechanical bridge plug was removed at the end of the intervention operation re-establishing reservoir communication and reservoir access.

In October 2015 the DC124 dual zone completion had a failed Baker Neptune (Gen-1) SCSSV replaced along with its 5.5-in 23-ppf 13Cr85 Tubing.  Prior to removal of the completion tubing string, the SCSSV was locked open and a surveillance run on wireline was made.  This consisted of a 3.00-in drift, run on S/L through to the bottom of the sand control screens in the M54 zone.  This drift run confirmed that there were no blockages through the bore of the completion. A prior 3.65-in drift run was unsuccessful due to a tight spot at ~17,150-ft.
The reservoir was isolated during the SCSSV and Tubing retrieval from the well via an inflatable mechanical bridge plug, so as to prevent fluid loss to the formation and possible formation damage.  The originally installed upper completion was removed via shearing of the Tubing Shear Latch (TSL) above the originally installed production packer.  This left a Polished Bore Receptacle (PBR) above the originally installed Production Packer.  This PBR served to receive the new seal assembly that would be installed beneath the new completion tubing string. 
A new tapered tubing string was installed consisting of 5.5-in 23-ppf 13Cr85 tubing x 4.5-in 15.1-ppf 13Cr85 tubing.  The 5.5-in tubing was only installed from the tubing hanger to the 10 ¾-in Tie-Back crossover on the production casing string.  The 4.5-in tubing was installed from the 10 ¾-in Tie-Back crossover through the 9 7/8-in production casing down to the PBR above the TSL.   
The new SCSSV was installed on the 5.5-in completion tubing to a depth of approximately 3,000-ft beneath the mud-line as per Atlantis Completion BOD.  This SCSSV was a Schlumberger TRC-II 10-ksi model with 4.437 "DB" profile.  
A new Schlumberger dual redundant gauge mandrel was installed with 2 gauges (redundant) each reading the tubing pressure and temperature.  Schlumberger Dual Check Injection Nipples (DCINs) were installed for chemical injection as per Atlantis Completions BOD.  A new Baker Premier Production Packer was installed above the TSL PBR.  
The production annulus (Annulus-A) was left with 9.1-ppg CaCl2 packer fluid, the production tubing was left with 6.5-ppg Base Oil.  Several attempts were made to remove the Mechanical bridge plug from the wellbore that were unsuccessful.  The bridge plug was finally released and fell down hole.  A retrieval tool with a 2-in OD was run in hole to the sump packer.  There was no indication of the bridge plug.  The bridge plug fell into the sump.  A pin from a clamp used to secure the Expro umbilical was lost downhole and never recovered.

The M40 was previously brought on 10/20/15 at 1,900 bopd (seperate APM/WAR), but after 3 days of steady production the PI began to drop from an initial 4 bopd/psi to 1.0 bopd/psi. The well was shut in 10/27/15 to establish a new SITP and analyze the PI decline, but from that point forward the well performance indicates that the A3 tubing is fully obstructed between the tubing pressure gauge and the M40 reservoir. Shakeouts after 10/21/15 showed 0% water in the A-3 production fluid. 

Slickline was mobilized 1/3/16 and tagged at 1,015' SLM. Sample bailer beat down to 1,157', but failed to grab sample. Dump bailed 4x 2.5 gallons of xylene, moving tag depth down to 1,203' SLM. RIH with sample bailer, grabbed sample at 1,312' SLM, discovered hydrate in sample bailer. Began pumping glycol into well with slickline test pump, alternating between pumping, bleeding, RIH with sample bailer to agitate and beat on plug, and dump bailing glycol. Over 7 day period got down to 3,240' SLM, then demobed slickline once progress stagnated. (Previous APM/WAR.)

Coil tubing was mobilized 2/28/16, and had successfully washed through the hydrate by 3/6/16. The M40 has been on production since 3/6/16, and was depleted to an estimated shut in bottom hole pressure of 5,952 psi at the DHPG, which is within 200 psi of the M50 SIBHP @ DHPG (5,854 psi). The down hole pressure gage (DHPG) has been providing unreliable data since 10/14, so all current pressure analysis has been based on the A3 Tubing Pressure (TP) gauge. (Previous APM/WAR.)

Slickline mobilized 4/6/16 to open the upper M50 sleeve and commingle production with the M40. During initial 2.25" gauge ring run, sat down at 9,751'.  RIH with 1.843" swedge and spang jars to try and clear blockage and recovered white rubbery substance on tools.  RIH with sample bailer to work the obstruction and while pulling out of the hole, slickline operator closed crown valve before tools were in lubricator, leaving 50' of wire and tool string. RIH with blind box to break wire off rope socket and tool string. RIH with wire grab but did not recover any wire. Forced to RDMO wireline equipment due to SIMOPS. (Previous APM/WAR.)

The objective for this operation was to mobilize wireline to fish wire and tool string, clear the blockage at 9,751' and then open the Upper M50 sleeve to commingle the M40 and M50 reservoirs and bring them on production together.

The well was not flowed back and shut-in. The well is stable and currently shut in, and will remain shut in until a rig workover can be performed. Both  smart  sleeves  are  closed  and  pressure  tested  to  1,000  psi  differential,  providing  an  additional  barrier to the reservoir.     
A riserless acid stimulation was performed 2/16/17-2/17/2017 and  completed pumping at 6:20 AM on 2/17/17. On the evening of 2/17/17, communication was detected between the tubing and annulus and was confirmed through further diagnostics. The lower smart sleeve was closed on 2/18/17 at 16:00 (note: the upper smart sleeve remained closed for the duration of the project), and then methanol was injected into the tubing to apply a 1,000 psi differential - during this period DHP1 (bottom hole tubing pressure) increased 1,000  psi,  however no response was seen on DHP2(upper zone) and DHP3(lower  zone), indicating the smart sleeves are sealing and have full integrity. Prior to the departure of the riserless stimulation vessel on 2/18/17‐ 2/19/17, the tree annulus cavity was pressurized to 10,000 psi. The pressure test held and an ROV inspection during the test indicated no leaks at or around the tree. A rig intervention is being planned, and the well will remain shut-in. A casing pressure departure was approved 3/3/17 for six months.
